# ceblar-20 v0.6

## Highlights

v0.6 hardens the v0.5 educational-kernel foundation with copy-on-write fork, range-based anonymous `mmap`/`munmap`, per-process descriptor inheritance and release hooks, zombie address-space reclamation on successful wait, a bounded IPv4/UDP loopback foundation, and an end-to-end ring-3 ELF fixture loaded from FAT32.

## Memory and process work

Fork now shares mapped user pages with read-only COW PTEs and physical-page reference counts. A write fault allocates a private page, copies the old contents through a temporary kernel mapping, updates the faulting PTE, and releases the shared reference. The boot self-test verifies parent/child write isolation. `SYS_MMAP` accepts a page-aligned address and byte length, rejects overlaps, rolls back partial allocation failures, and `SYS_MUNMAP` releases every page in a validated range.

The process manager now copies descriptor state on fork, releases non-standard descriptors at exit, and reclaims a waited child’s address space. The frame-aware wait path remains compatible with the IRQ/syscall return ABI.

## Storage, exec, and network

The FAT32 test generator installs both `HELLO.TXT` and `HELLO.ELF`. QEMU attaches the image as an IDE disk; the kernel mounts FAT32, queues a new ring-3 process from `hda/HELLO.ELF`, and captures `disk: hello` alongside the embedded init’s `user: hello`. The network foundation supplies packet structures, Internet checksum calculation, ARP-cache storage, and a bounded loopback queue. It does not yet claim hardware NIC support.

## Verification

```sh
make clean
make -j2
grub-file --is-x86-multiboot2 build/kernel.elf
make test
```

The regression suite passes both no-disk and FAT32-disk boots. The disk run emits `vmm: COW self-test passed`, `net: IPv4/UDP foundation ready`, `fat32: HELLO.TXT read ok`, `exec: disk ELF queued`, `disk: hello`, `user: hello`, and both worker completion markers.

## Remaining boundaries

The kernel remains a small freestanding teaching system. Network hardware drivers, ARP/IPv4/UDP/TCP sockets, file-backed mappings, VMA interval metadata, process-slot reuse, orphan adoption, reference-counted open-file descriptions, and complete syscall/userland test coverage remain future work. The COW, mmap, descriptor, wait, and disk-exec paths are implemented and smoke-tested but are not presented as production-grade.
